bullets: Reef-conservation policy functions as a planetary-scale systems problem — ignoring systemic feedback loops leads to repeated, ineffective interventions.
Most operational dive safety hinges on avoiding pushing tired teams — the real risk is not fatigue itself but the decision-making under fatigue.
Risk management on extended dives is primarily about exit planning — effective planning ensures predictable, safe termination of dives.
Adopting GoPro in dive workflows reveals hidden trade-offs — the tool's integration makes the cost of delay or data loss more visible.
Using Suunto in dive operations exposes the second-order effect of real-time data — teams often overlook that data flow impacts decision timing and team coordination.
The framing of a problem determines which trade-offs are made visible — a systems perspective reveals that policy and safety are shaped by how questions are structured.
Failure in marine conservation often stems from rebuilding efforts annually — this happens when systemic feedback loops are ignored rather than integrated.
Running a single idea for two weeks enables iterative improvement — the key is sustained practice, not immediate perfection.
